items.title: 'Devoted father and gentleman': Tributes flow for shark attack victim
items.description: The wife of a 38-year-old Perth man who died in a shark attack off the coast of Rottnest Island in Western Australia on Saturday describes him as a devoted father and avid spearfisherman.

items.title: Treasurer stands by CGT changes affecting shares and crypto
items.description: Jim Chalmers says it is better for young people to invest based on economic rather than tax outcomes, and argued they can still access negative gearing by buying up new homes.

items.title: Labor claims victory in Queensland's Stafford by-election
items.description: Labor candidate Luke Richmond claims victory over the LNP's Fiona Hammond in a tight race in the north Brisbane electorate of Stafford.

items.title: Qantas plane diverted after passenger allegedly bites flight attendant
items.description: Fellow passengers are believed to have assisted after a flight attendant was allegedly bitten on plane travelling between Melbourne and the US, with the plane diverted to Tahiti.

items.title: Protesters march at Nakba Day rallies around Australia
items.description: Crowds gather at rallies around the country to commemorate the anniversary of the Nakba, a day that recognises the mass displacement of Palestinians in 1948.

items.title: From Euro-pop to Euro-slop, the key moments from Eurovision as Delta makes Australia proud
items.description: Slept through Eurovision this year? Here's what you missed from Europe's favourite song contest, with boycotts, ballads and a Bulgarian belter called Bangaranga making headlines.

items.title: Live: Giants take control with third-quarter surge at Perth Stadium
items.description: Round 10 of the AFL concludes as West Coast welcomes GWS to Perth Stadium, after St Kilda makes light work of Richmond at Docklands. Follow live.

items.title: Live: NSW suffer major Origin blow, Warriors thrash Broncos in Brisbane
items.description: South Sydney and NSW star Latrell Mitchell is ruled out of State of Origin I after aggravating his back injury during Magic Round. Follow live.

items.title: You could hear a pin drop when Rob revealed why he fought a fire tax
items.description: Every time farmer and volunteer firefighter Rob Armstrong gets a call to battle a bushfire, something inside says not to do it. But he goes anyway. He knows what it’s like to be trapped in the flames and rescued by volunteers.

items.title: Ebola kills 87 people as cases continue to rise in Congo
items.description: At least 87 deaths have been reported in Congo's new Ebola disease outbreak, as health authorities warn the strain "has no vaccine, no specific treatment".

items.title: How Pokémon cards are fuelling crime in Melbourne
items.description: Rare Pokémon cards can sell for hundreds or even thousands of dollars, with a record sale of one Pikachu card going for over $22 million earlier this year.

items.title: Sydney lawyer was stressed out by her mortgage so she sold up and bought a van
items.description: Phoebe Macdougall says she hated living with a mortgage, so she is trying van life instead.

items.title: AI psychosis is on the rise and experts are sounding the alarm
items.description: Rodrigues thought an AI chatbot could help him escape poverty and build wealth. Instead, he became trapped in a spiral of delusion and dependence.

items.title: Six shops ordered to shut under new illegal tobacco laws
items.description: More than 140,000 illegal cigarettes have been seized and six stores ordered to close down, days after Western Australia's new tobacco laws came into force.

items.title: Love story: How a punk grandma and an Aussie rocker fell in love
items.description: Singer/guitarist Mick Medew and self-proclaimed punk grandma Ursula Collie were in their mid-50s when they met and bonded over a mutual love of live music. A decade on, they're musical and life partners.

items.title: ‘I can still feel him’: Gurrumul’s posthumous honour brings pride for family
items.description: Nearly a decade since his death, Gurrumul is set to be inducted into the ARIA Hall of Fame, bringing pride and reflection to a remote part of Australia.

items.title: Test your homophones and your Gen Alpha slang
items.description: Are you ready to test your spelling skills like your little lunch depends on it? Come on in.

items.title: 'No-one really questioned why' Olympic gymnast missed periods
items.description: Alexandra Kiroi-Bogatyreva trained up to 10 hours a day, six days a week, often without the proper nutrition. She wants others to know what that can do to the body.

items.title: Why some Australian homebuyers are turning to Islamic financing
items.description: When Wildan decided to buy a property he didn't even consider a conventional loan. Instead, he opted for a niche option that caters to a growing segment of Australia's population.

items.title: What life was like before the NDIS and why mistakes can't be repeated
items.description: The states are once again on the hook for disability services due to the Commonwealth's drastic NDIS cuts. Can the mistakes of the past be avoided?

items.title: Hobart military barracks slated for housing development
items.description: Up to 1,000 new homes could be built on the site of a military barracks in Hobart, under a state-federal redevelopment agreement.

items.title: The budget hammers the final nail into the coffin of the Howard-era tax breaks
items.description: At the turn of the century, "aspiration" described Australians who wanted to put their kids into private school and university, and to build their wealth by getting an investment property or two. Today, it means something humbler; millions of younger Australians simply aspire to own a home one day, to have some shelter.

items.title: The darkness of a Tasmanian town's night sky could be protected
items.description: The northern Tasmanian town of Ross is working to protect its night sky, a years-long process that would see it formally recognised for its darkness and clarity.

items.title: From cask to car, could red wine be Australia's next fuel?
items.description: Australia's wine industry is investigating whether its current 263 million litre glut of wine would be better used as biofuel to power cars, trucks or even aircraft.

items.title: China quietly turns off supply of world's most used industrial chemical
items.description: Amid disruption from the Iran war, China has banned exports of sulphuric acid, a crucial component used to treat drinking water, refine petroleum and make batteries, clothing and phosphate fertilisers.
